headline: How much longer do I have to wait for my soulmate?
note: generated from REVIEW-new-voice.md — not a wired draft

a: You turned the Magician. You couldn't tell one back from another, and you took the one who came ready.
Look at his table. The tools are out, and none of them is put away.
You asked how much longer you have to wait. I keep going back to that table — all out, none of it in use.
Still, nobody has come. And the waiting is what you want measured.
Something turns up right when this would start moving. I don't think it started with you.
Let me look closer at what's behind this…
b: You turned the Hanged Man. You couldn't see them, and you took the one hung from a single rope.
Look at the rope. One ankle, and the rest of him swings free.
You asked how much longer you have to wait. One rope is doing all of it.
And yet nobody has come. And what you want from me is a number.
The hold is even — it doesn't pull, and it doesn't slacken. I don't think any of it began with you.
Let me look closer at what's holding this…
c: You turned the Fool. Nothing showed through the backs, and you chose the one already stepping out.
Look at his feet. One foot is up, and the other is under him.
You asked how much longer you have to wait. The step in this one is already being taken.
But nobody has come. And you're the one asking how much longer.
Something stands right where that step lands. I don't think it began with you.
Let me look closer at what's holding this…
